title: Symmetry and Monotonicity of y = sqrt(-x)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Describe the graph of y = sqrt(-x), state whether it has any symmetry, and specify the intervals where the function is increasing or decreasing.

steps.title: Find the Domain and Check Symmetry
steps.explanation: Because the domain (-inf, 0] is only a single half-line and is not symmetric about x = 0, the graph has no symmetry (neither y-axis, x-axis, nor origin symmetry).
steps.why: For a function to be even or odd, its domain must be symmetric about the origin (x in D implies -x in D).

steps.title: Test Monotonicity on (-inf, 0]
steps.explanation: For any x_1 < x_2 <= 0, negating reverses the inequality to -x_1 > -x_2 >= 0, and taking the principal square root yields sqrt(-x_1) > sqrt(-x_2).
steps.why: Composing the strictly increasing function sqrt(u) with the strictly decreasing linear function u = -x produces a strictly decreasing function.

steps.title: Summarize Graph and Intervals
steps.explanation: The curve lies in Quadrant II and descends continuously from left to right, passing through (-4, 2) and (-1, 1) to terminate at (0, 0).
steps.why: Every increase in x on (-inf, 0] reduces the value of the radicand -x.
